answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy starts with a per-identity bond staked before an agent may transact or vote. Each new identity must lock the same minimum bond, so one operator running a thousand puppets pays a thousand times, and the capital stays frozen. Reputation accrues on a shared ledger from settled work, and a fresh address starts at zero, so splitting one record into many does not multiply trust. Witnesses form a grove of independent attestors that audit each other. A lone agent is a dune the tide erases; a bonded peer network is a steady signal forgery cannot fake.
